lf-playground.description: A preview with controls, where the user tunes one configuration and sends it.
lf-playground.x-instructions: Frame the question with `lf-ask` when its context lives outside the playground. A page module can add structured values with `registerContributor(name, defaultSnapshot, {read, apply})`, calling the returned notifier after each gesture, and write the instruction from those values with one `registerInstructionProvider(values => text)`. To give the task's values an exact schema, redeclare the complete `lf-playground` entry in `page/registry.json`.
lf-playground.x-example:
Which notification should we build?

Banner

The real banner responds to the shared controls.

Status strip

The real status strip responds to the same controls.

Build the notification with corners. Replace the notification component and show me its browser test.

lf-playground-control.description: One typed input in a playground.
lf-playground-control.x-instructions: Use a stable `name` for the submitted field and a `label` for the control. Write its initial `value` as a string: a finite number for range, true or false for toggle, one child's value for choice, a six-digit hex color for color, or any text for text. A range needs `max`; `min`, `step` and `unit` are optional. Only a choice control contains lf-playground-choice children. A control that changes the whole preview, as most do, is a direct child of lf-playground and appears in its rail. When the preview holds several items that each take their own settings, write each item's controls inside lf-playground-preview beside that item, where they appear as written.

lf-playground-choice.description: One labeled value offered by a playground choice control.
lf-playground-choice.x-instructions: Use value for the submitted value and label for the words the user sees.

lf-playground-preset.description: A named partial playground configuration the user can apply at once.
lf-playground-preset.x-instructions: Include settings only for values the preset changes; unspecified controls keep their current values.

lf-playground-setting.description: One control value applied by a playground preset.
lf-playground-setting.x-instructions: Set for to a control in the same playground and write value in that control's authored string form.

lf-playground-preview.description: The candidates the user operates in a playground.
lf-playground-preview.x-instructions: For an A/B comparison, mount both candidates here and drive them from one state, as the playground package's author instructions describe. Page CSS can read the `--playground-NAME` properties and `data-playground-NAME` attributes. A page module can read `values`, listen for `lf-playground-change`, handle gestures and computed state, and load vendored or page-media assets from the page's origin.

lf-playground-output.description: The task instruction displayed by a playground and sent with the chosen configuration.
lf-playground-output.x-instructions: Write a self-contained task rather than a value dump. Insert lf-playground-value where scalar selections make it more precise; use a registered instruction provider for prose that depends on structured or conditional values.

lf-playground-value.description: A live scalar value embedded in a playground instruction.
lf-playground-value.x-instructions: Set for to a control in the enclosing playground. Numeric values already include the control's unit.
